title: One evidence record on a skills-lexicon entry (v0 draft)
$comment: Evidence attaches to one claim of one entry. A pass that runs elsewhere (a search, a page read, a Wikipedia dump on a cluster) hands back records of this shape, keyed by the entry's id. Rules that need the whole entry (every claim of a machine-drafted entry has a drafted record; a reviewed entry has a backing record for every claim) are checked by tools/lexicon.py, not here.

field.description: The claim this is about. One of: kind, definition, certification, certification_scope, language_type, variant:<normalised label>, relation:<type>:<target id>, verb:<normalised verb>.

by.description: model:<model id>, human:<name>, or source:<name of an outside record or dataset, such as enwiki-20261001>. A source can match a claim but cannot draft one.

action.description: drafted: someone proposed the claim. checked: someone checked it. matched_source: the claim was matched to an outside record.

kind.description: What kind of source a matched_source record points to. issuer: the body that awards the credential. regulator or standard: a body that sets or lists it. onet, bls, esco, sfia: an occupational taxonomy. job-postings: job listings that ask for it.

verification.description: How much was actually verified, required for matched_source. page-read: someone opened the page and the quote is from it. dump-match: matched against a downloaded dataset. search-results-only: only a search result was seen. Only page-read and dump-match back a claim.

organization.description: Who attests it: the organization behind the source, with a link to the organization itself (not to one page). Required for matched_source. For a certification this is the official body that says the credential exists.

ref.description: Required for matched_source: a URL, an identifier in the dataset (for example wikidata:Q4686912) or an ad id.

run.description: The run label of the pass that produced the record.

note.description: Short free text: the basis of a draft, or a short quote from the source.

flag.description: Asks a person to look. A flag never backs or contradicts a claim.

match.description: Optional detail when the source is a dataset matched by a script.

dataset_id.description: The record's id in the dataset, for example a Wikipedia page id or a Wikidata QID.

score.description: A similarity score for name-similarity matches.

count.description: For job-postings: how many postings in the dataset ask for it.

categories.description: What the dataset says the record is: Wikipedia categories or Wikidata classes. For the claim `certification` this is the evidence that the thing is a credential.
